channel.title: Wildcard Watch: exploited right now
channel.description: Vulnerabilities that attackers are actively exploiting, plus breaches and supply-chain attacks, with the fix status and first step for each. By Wildcard Group.

item.title: Patch now (update): TeamViewer Flaw Could Let Malicious Hosts Take Over Support Technicians’ Machines
item.description:
TeamViewer (multiple products): Memory corruption (possible RCE) · pre-auth · remote · user interaction · exploited · fix: 15.83, 15.64.10 (Legacy Windows 7 & 8), 14.7.48868 (Windows)

First step: Update the affected TeamViewer products to the fixed version for your release line (for example 15.83, 15.64.10 (Legacy Windows 7 & 8) or 14.7.48868 (Windows)).

An integer overflow in the remote-control screen processing component of TeamViewer clients (Full Client, Portable and Remote Control App) prior to version 15.83 may allow a malicious remote host to cause a denial of service or, depending on the platform, potentially execute arbitrary code with the privileges of the viewer process.

High · Fix available · CVE-2026-111585

item.title: Act now (update): Ivanti Connect Secure: 2 flaws exploited together
item.description:

First step: Update Ivanti Connect Secure to 25.1.1.3 or later.

High · Check vendor · CVE-2026-111357, CVE-2026-118527

item.title: Patch now: Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Controller and Manager: Authentication Bypass
item.description:
Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Controller and Manager: Authentication bypass · internet-facing · exploited from day 0 · fix: 20.9.8.2, 20.12.5.3, 20.15.4.2

First step: Update Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Controller and Manager to the fixed version for your release line (for example 20.9.8.2, 20.12.5.3 or 20.15.4.2).

Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Controller, formerly SD-WAN vSmart, and Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager, formerly SD-WAN vManage, contain an authentication bypass vulnerability could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to bypass authentication and obtain administrative privileges on an affected system. This vulnerability exists because the peering authentication mechanism in an affected system is not working properly. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by sending crafted requests to an affected system. A successful exploit could allow the attacker to log in to an affected Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Controller as an internal, high-privileged, non-root user account. Using this account, the attacker could access NETCONF, which would then allow the attacker to manipulate network configuration for the SD-WAN fabric.

Critical · Fix available · CVE-2026-20127

item.title: Patch now: Linux Kernel: Missing Initialization of a Variable
item.description:
Linux Kernel: exploited · fix: 5.10.257, 5.15.208, 6.1.174

First step: Install your Linux distribution's kernel update. The upstream fix is in 5.10.257, 5.15.208 or 6.1.174.

Linux Kernel contains a missing initialization of a variable vulnerability that could allow for unintended modification of page-cache-backed data via failure to preserve the shared-fragment marker during socket buffer coalescing, causing ESP input processing to decrypt shared fragments in place. This vulnerability can be chained with CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 to implant PHP webshells and run commands as root.

High · Fix available · CVE-2026-46300, CVE-2026-98432
